chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ibrahim ibn Mihzam, from Al-Qasim ibn Al-Walid, who said:
I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the bones of the elephant, its oils, and its combs. He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem with it.'

key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ بِهَا: there is no problem with it (permissible/pure)

ai.seo_question: Are elephant bones and combs considered ritually pure in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this concise narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) confirms the permissibility of using elephant bones, oils, and combs, addressing specific concerns regarding ritual purity (*taharah*) in daily life. This ruling reflects the Shia jurisprudential principle that animal parts are inherently pure unless explicitly proven otherwise, reinforcing the ease (*yusr*) in Islamic law regarding non-sacred creatures. The mention of 'combs' (*amshat*) highlights the practical application of these materials in personal hygiene, linking physical cleanliness to spiritual purity.
